short: Both front ends are new to their 2014 populations but transfer outside designs without repetition (M06 standard); stream weights and depth are tuned on the test words (M12 behind).
position: Both learned front ends of the decoder (M06) [@noda2015audiovisual] are new to their populations, 0 of 55 prior AVSR studies naming a learned audio denoiser and 0 of 106 prior lip-reading studies a 2D CNN (pattern match, Appendix), but each moves an outside design ([@feng2014speech], [@duchnowski1994see]) and neither gain is repeated, so M06 is standard. The same authors' [concurrent] Interspeech paper [@noda2014lipreading] reports the same visual pipeline on the same corpus without mention in the journal text. Evaluation (M12) is behind on one point: stream weights and autoencoder depth are chosen on the 40 test words, whereas read priors tune weights on held-out data [@papandreou2009adaptive], [@potamianos2003audiovisual]. As the paper states (Sec. 5.3), the "additional 10 %" at 0 dB (Sec. 6.5) is thus a best-of-weights result from one run.
